header.purpose: Canonical cross-language approval binding conformance specification. Integration (CP7 Lane A/B) must verify that the TypeScript ApprovalBindingPayload and the Rust approval binding digest agree 1:1 through these fields and canonicalization rules. This document defines data contracts and rules only; it intentionally contains no implementation commands.
header.conformance_rule: The Rust approval binding digest MUST be computed over exactly the canonical form defined here. The TS ApprovalBindingPayload MUST serialize to the same canonical form. Any field present on one side and absent on the other, or any canonicalization divergence, is a CP7 integration failure.

canonical_binding_fields.type_contract: string, canonical lowercase identifier pattern (adapter + capability)
canonical_binding_fields.description: Stable identity of the binding the approval covers

canonical_binding_fields.type_contract: string, one-way digest of the canonical plan content (excludes approval fields)
canonical_binding_fields.description: Binds approval to the exact plan content; any plan mutation invalidates the approval
canonical_binding_fields.rust_side: verified against re-computed digest at spawn

canonical_binding_fields.description: The exact risk the actor approved; the Authority must reject any plan whose compiled binding risk exceeds this snapshot
canonical_binding_fields.rust_side: re-validated against the compiled binding declaration

canonical_binding_fields.type_contract: string, canonical provider.resource.action lowercase dotted id

canonical_binding_fields.description: Version pin of the capability; a version mismatch invalidates the approval
The concrete adapter implementation being approved

canonical_binding_fields.type_contract: string, NFC-normalized, canonical subject key (e.g. owner/repo#number)
canonical_binding_fields.description: The exact decision subject; cross-subject reuse is forbidden

canonical_binding_fields.type_contract: object, JSON-safe, finite values only, arrays strictly ordered, bounded size
canonical_binding_fields.description: The exact normalized inputs approved; any input mutation invalidates the approval
canonical_binding_fields.rust_side: digest input; re-hash comparison at spawn

canonical_binding_fields.type_contract: array of qualified evidence record ids, strictly ordered, each resolvable to Guard-run output
canonical_binding_fields.description: The qualified evidence records that existed at approval time; post-approval evidence mutation or stale replacement invalidates the approval

canonical_binding_fields.type_contract: string, RFC3339 UTC (Z offset), strictly in the future at grant time and at spawn time
canonical_binding_fields.description: Mandatory bounded lifetime of the grant

canonical_binding_fields.type_contract: string, exact-match actor identity, never confusable-normalized
canonical_binding_fields.description: The actor who granted approval; the Authority must verify actor authority >= authority_required
Instant the grant was issued; used for TTL and audit

canonical_binding_fields.type_contract: string, the exact policy version in force at grant time
canonical_binding_fields.description: A policy downgrade after grant must be detected; the Authority re-checks against the current policy version

canonical_binding_fields.type_contract: integer, finite safe integer, within contract bounds
canonical_binding_fields.description: Execution timeout bound captured in the binding

canonical_binding_fields.type_contract: string digest or null, exactly mirroring plan content
canonical_binding_fields.description: If the plan carries a verification plan it is part of the bound content; swapping it invalidates the approval

canonical_binding_fields.type_contract: string digest or null, exactly mirroring plan content
canonical_binding_fields.description: If the plan carries a rollback plan it is part of the bound content; swapping it invalidates the approval

canonical_binding_fields.type_contract: string, opaque, unique, bounded length, never falsy-defaulted
canonical_binding_fields.description: Store key of the grant record

canonical_binding_fields.type_contract: string, opaque reference to the stored token material (never the raw token)
canonical_binding_fields.description: Points at the stored secret; raw token must never appear in the binding or logs

canonical_binding_fields.type_contract: string, salted one-way digest of the stored token
canonical_binding_fields.description: Allows validation of the referenced token without exposing it; unsalted or reversible digests are forbidden

canonicalization_rules.rule: Objects are canonicalized key-order insensitively at every nesting level; equivalent objects with different key order produce identical digests.
Arrays are strictly ordered; array element reordering changes the digest and fails closed where schema order is meaningful.
Strings are Unicode NFC-normalized before canonicalization; visually equivalent forms must not create aliases.
Timestamps use exactly one canonical encoding: RFC3339 UTC with Z offset (or +00:00 normalized to Z); epoch and offset variants are rejected.
Numbers must be finite JSON safe integers; NaN, Infinity, BigInt, negative zero, and values beyond 2^53 fail closed.
undefined is not a JSON value: required fields must be present with explicit values, optional fields use explicit null.
Control characters (NUL, CR, LF, ESC, etc.) are rejected or serialized as JSON escapes; raw control bytes never enter the digest.
Booleans and strings are strictly typed: "true"/"false" strings never coerce to booleans, and numbers never coerce to strings.
Number representation is single-form: 1.0 and 1 serialize identically or the non-canonical form is rejected; "1" never aliases 1.
Unknown/extra fields fail closed: nothing may be silently dropped from the digest, and prototype-like keys (__proto__, constructor, prototype) never affect object semantics.
Duplicate JSON keys fail closed before parsing semantics can diverge between TS and Rust.
Empty strings are distinct values, never treated as missing, and must survive canonicalization unchanged.
The digest is computed over the canonical serialized form, not over raw input text; formatting, whitespace, and key order of the raw payload must not matter.
Any divergence between the TS and Rust canonical encoders for identical logical payloads is a CP7 integration failure (deterministic, byte-identical digests are required).

security_requirements: Schema-valid is not approved: the durable store record must exist, match all binding fields, and be live (not expired, revoked, denied, or consumed).
The Authority re-validates plan risk against the compiled binding at spawn; Brain-side risk claims are never authoritative.
Grant consumption happens atomically before spawn, never after; consume and spawn are protected against TOCTOU.
The ledger is durable and crash-safe; corrupt or partial store state fails closed and never resets silently to empty.
Actors with authority below authority_required can never grant; LLM/Skill/Provider output can never grant.
No raw token material appears in bindings, digests, logs, errors, or audit summaries.
Approval for plan A can never authorize plan B; every binding field above is compared, not just plan_id.

integration_authority.authority_statement: This section is the CP7 integration freeze. The Lane C draft sections above remain preserved as the original design input; where the draft conflicts with this frozen section, this section is authoritative for the implemented V1. The integration explicitly did NOT execute a wire-contract migration to add evidence_guard_run_id, so the cross-language binding binds evidence_coverage_digest only.

evidence_boundary.decision: evidence_coverage_digest is bound; evidence_guard_run_id is NOT part of the cross-language binding
evidence_boundary.rationale: CP6 Guard lineage is owned by the Brain Evidence authority. The native Approval/Broker can directly observe the authoritative coverage snapshot carried by the server-owned ExecutionPlan (evidence_coverage_snapshot), and the existing ExecutionPlan wire has no evidence_guard_run_id field. Adding it would require an explicit TS ExecutionPlanSchema + Rust ExecutionPlanWire + fixture/test migration.
evidence_boundary.brain_authority_boundary: Brain owns evidence qualification: EvidenceEligibilityService materializes coverage exclusively from CP6 Guard-run output; callers can never pass coverage, guard_run_id or a guard fake. Brain ApprovalRequestRecord may keep evidence_guard_run_id for audit/provenance only.
evidence_boundary.native_authority_boundary: The native Broker does NOT re-prove CP6 GuardRunStore lineage. It independently validates: compiled capability risk, the approval grant record, the exact plan semantics digest (which includes evidence_coverage_digest), expiry, and single-use ledger state.

canonical_binding_fields_v1.type: string digest or explicit JSON null
string digest or explicit JSON null
string (RFC3339 UTC, exact form bound verbatim)
string (RFC3339 UTC, exact form bound verbatim)

integration_authority.excluded_rationale: Lifecycle fields (state/approval/required_approval) are not "the frozen execution semantics the actor approved". token_reference/token_digest are opaque store references, not binding semantics. evidence_guard_run_id is excluded per the evidence-boundary decision above. The TS payload rejects these keys strictly; the Rust payload does not emit them.
integration_authority.null_semantics: expires_at absent and verification_plan/rollback_plan null are canonically encoded as explicit JSON null in both languages (single encoding per semantic).

canonical_json_rules.encoding: UTF-8; SHA-256 over the canonical serialized form
canonical_json_rules.key_order: object keys sorted by UTF-16 code unit order (JS-compatible, matches JSON.stringify + explicit sort); arrays keep order
canonical_json_rules.string_escaping: JS JSON.stringify-compatible escaping (including U+2028/U+2029 and control characters)
canonical_json_rules.unicode: NO normalization. Combining and precomposed forms digest differently (documented, tested). This supersedes draft CANON-003.
canonical_json_rules.numbers: strict subset: JSON-safe finite numbers, |value| <= Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER, no exponent notation, at most 6 fractional digits, fixed-point only; -0 canonicalizes to 0; 1 and 1.0 both canonicalize to "1"; NaN/Infinity rejected fail-closed. This supersedes draft CANON-005/CANON-009 details.
canonical_json_rules.duplicate_keys: rejected at the typed parse layer (strict serialization); duplicate JSON object keys cannot reach the digest
canonical_json_rules.timestamps: bound as exact RFC3339 strings with no normalization; two encodings of the same instant digest differently (documented, tested). This supersedes draft CANON-004.

durable_replay_semantics.model: write-ahead fail-closed ordered reservation: 1. accept (approval record validated, binding digest re-computed) -> 2. durably reserve plan_id -> 3. durably consume approval -> 4. spawn. Availability loss is acceptable; double effect is not.
durable_replay_semantics.approval_store: persistent JSON store with strict record validation (hex digests, plan_id format, token format, lifetime <= 15m, state consistency); lock acquired at open
durable_replay_semantics.plan_ledger: persistent write-ahead ledger (Accepted/Reserved phases); corrupt ledger => degraded fail-closed, never reset empty
durable_replay_semantics.cross_process: exclusive OS file lock (LockFileEx on Windows, flock on unix) taken for the store lifetime; a second broker on the same store opens degraded. Documented enforceability: single-instance authority plus fail-closed lock.
durable_replay_semantics.crash_sequencing: fault points: BeforePlanReserve, AfterPlanReserve, BeforeApprovalConsume, AfterApprovalConsume, BeforeSpawn. Every fault point tested: after restart the same plan can never spawn again (replayable_after_restart = 0).
durable_replay_semantics.spawn_failure: never unconsumes the approval and never unreserves the plan; a retry requires a new plan + new approval
durable_replay_semantics.single_use: approval single-use (consume once), plan single-use across restart (reserved/executed ledger state)
durable_replay_semantics.audit: consumed/denied/revoked grants are retained as audit records with who/when/authority/policy/binding_digest/status/consumed_at

concurrency.multi_broker_same_store: second broker instance on the same store opens degraded (OS lock); cross-process guarantee is the fail-closed lock, not lock-free coordination

approval_ttl.plan_expiry: approval expiry must not exceed plan expiry; plans without explicit expires_at follow the native broker default TTL with no conflict documented

brain_restart_semantics.authorization_store: memory-only (Lane A); Brain restart invalidates its pending/ready authorization state
brain_restart_semantics.native_grants: unused native grants remain in the durable store until expiry/revoke/consume; they cannot be used externally because generic execute IPC=false and no public plan submission path exists in CP7
brain_restart_semantics.limitation: Brain restart does not automatically revoke native durable grants (not implemented); recorded as CP7 limitation / CP9 integration requirement

integration_authority.cp9_bridge_requirement: The CP9 trusted Brain<->Tauri bridge must submit the server-owned current ExecutionPlan/approval lifecycle object; it must never forward an arbitrary WebView-constructed plan to the Broker. No such public bridge is implemented in CP7.
remaining_limitations: Brain AuthorizationStore is memory-only (restart semantics above).
Cross-process coordination relies on the fail-closed OS lock + single-instance authority assumption, documented rather than a lock-free distributed protocol.
No Approval UI / owner interaction surface exists until CP9.
Approval authority is the local native ApprovalStore; no network crypto protocol (no JWT/asymmetric signatures) is introduced by design.
